goal: Extend packages/core/src/pricing (currently spot-price-only, per MainScreenView.tsx's own deferral comment) with a historical price time series and a portfolio-value estimator over that series, so a caller can compute approximate total portfolio value at points in the past without reconstructing historical token balances from on-chain activity.

requirements.statement: Historical portfolio value is estimated as current/latest known balance times historical price at each point in the series (the confirmed approximation) -- never true historical balance reconstruction from on-chain activity. This is a deliberate scope boundary confirmed with the user, not a shortcut to flag as debt.

If a token has no price data for a given timestamp from the price source (gap in the series, unsupported coin id, fetch failure), priceAt must return 0 for that timestamp so the token contributes 0 to the total at that point -- never skip the token, never throw, and never fabricate a plausible non-zero price. This is an explicit exception to this project's general HONESTY rule (surface unavailable as null/unavailable, never as 0) -- the user confirmed 0-contribution is the intended behavior specifically for this per-timestamp series case, distinct from pricing's existing getUsdPrice/getUsdPriceWithFallback (spot price), which still return null on failure and are unaffected by this rule.

Historical price fetching follows the same direct-source, fallback-on-failure pattern getUsdPriceWithFallback already establishes (CoinGecko direct first, CoinPaprika direct second, no server of this project's own proxying either) -- reuse or closely mirror that pattern rather than inventing a new one. No new external provider is introduced.

Ranges to support at minimum: 24H, 7D, 1M, 1Y, ALL (matching wallet-main-screen.html's range tabs) -- the exact granularity returned per range (e.g. hourly vs daily points) is a build-time detail this layer decides, informed by what the underlying price source actually returns at each range, not fixed here.

A new exported function (e.g. getHistoricalUsdPrices or equivalent) returns a time-ordered series of {timestamp, usd} points for a supported coin id and range, reusing the existing CoinGeckoId/CoinPaprikaId types where they already fit.

estimateHistoricalPortfolioValue exists with exactly the signature and reduce-based body confirmed with the user (tokens: { balance: number; priceAt: (timestamp: number) => number }[], timestamp: number) => number, and is unit-tested for: multiple tokens summing correctly, a token whose priceAt returns 0 for a given timestamp contributing 0 (not erroring, not being excluded), and an empty tokens array returning 0.

pnpm vitest run pricing passes, including new tests for the historical series fetch (mocked fetchImpl, same pattern as pricing.pricing.test.ts's existing tests) and for estimateHistoricalPortfolioValue; pnpm tsc -p packages/core --noEmit passes; no chrome.*/window/document dependency is introduced (pure, injectable fetchImpl, same as the rest of this module).
